canonical_statement: For the standard Gaussian probability measure gamma on finite-dimensional Euclidean space and every sufficiently regular real function f for which the displayed quantities exist, Ent_gamma(f^2) is at most twice the integral of the squared Euclidean norm of the gradient of f.
canonical_formula: integral (f^2 * log(f^2)) dgamma - m * log(m) <= 2 * integral ||grad f||^2 dgamma, where m = integral f^2 dgamma
domain_and_universes: provisional: dimension n : Nat; f : EuclideanSpace Real (Fin n) -> Real; proposition in Lean universe 0
quantifiers: f : EuclideanSpace Real (Fin n) -> Real satisfying the statement-phase regularity and integrability predicate
hypotheses: gamma is the standard centered Gaussian probability measure with identity covariance
f^2 and f^2 log(f^2) are integrable, with the zero-log-zero convention
boundary_cases: f = 0 gives both sides zero under the zero-log-zero convention
constant f gives zero entropy and zero energy
dimension zero must not introduce a normalization exception

alternate_encodings.target: normalized form with integral f^2 dgamma = 1
abstract Wiener space / Dirichlet form formulation

excluded_variants: No manifold, Bernoulli/discrete, modified, defective, or unspecified-measure log-Sobolev inequality is the canonical root.
